faq.label: Operational Honesty
faq.title: What FlightAgent Does and Does Not Promise
faq.subtitle: Clear expectations matter. FlightAgent is decision intelligence and periodic monitoring, not an airline operations feed.

checks.a: Booked trips and tracked itineraries are checked on scheduled monitoring cycles. The dashboard shows the latest monitoring snapshot when data is available.

systems.q: Does FlightAgent use live airline systems?
systems.a: FlightAgent does not claim airline-grade operational access. It uses available provider data and internal monitoring records to surface practical risk signals.

pricing.q: Are price signals estimated or live?
pricing.a: Fare context may be estimated or snapshot-based depending on available data. We label stale or unavailable data instead of implying real-time certainty.

delayed.q: What happens if monitoring is delayed?
delayed.a: Delayed or stale monitoring should be shown as an operational state, not hidden behind reassuring copy.

delivery.a: Detected events and notification attempts are tracked separately. Delivery can be retried, fail, or remain pending depending on provider response.

AboutPage.subtitle: Trip decision intelligence for long-haul travelers.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.content: FlightAgent helps travelers understand itinerary quality before booking and monitor booked trips afterward with transparent, scheduled checks. We focus on risk, route structure, fare context, and advisor-style recommendations rather than acting as an OTA or promising real-time airline operations.

story.title: Our Story
story.content: FlightAgent was built for travelers who need more than a cheap-price sort. Long-haul itineraries can fail through tight connections, self-transfers, stale data, or poor rebooking options, so our product is designed around decision clarity and honest monitoring state.
